notes.meaning: John sees an amazing sign in the sky of a woman shining with heavenly light. She represents the church, God's faithful family, clothed in the glory of Christ like bright sunshine. The moon under her feet shows she is lifted above changing earthly things, and the crown of twelve stars points to the twelve apostles whose preaching guides believers.

differ.view: The woman represents the nation of Israel, because the imagery of the sun, moon, and twelve stars matches Joseph's dream of the twelve tribes in Genesis.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The woman is understood primarily as Mary, the mother of Jesus, who was taken up bodily into heaven, while also representing Israel and the church.

notes.meaning: The woman cries out in deep pain as she is about to give birth. This shows the intense longing and prayers of God's ancient people as they waited for the promised Savior to arrive. It also pictures the hard struggles the faithful community endured before their deliverance came.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Because Mary gave birth without physical labor pains, these birth pangs represent her spiritual agony when Jesus died on the cross.

notes.meaning: A second sign appears showing a huge fiery red dragon. This monster represents Satan working through cruel earthly powers like the pagan Roman Empire. His seven heads and ten horns show vast earthly strength and divided kingdoms, while the crowns on his heads show his proud claim to rule the fallen world.

The dragon sweeps a third of the stars out of the sky with his tail, picturing Satan dragging down angels or seducing church teachers into error. He crouches directly in front of the mother, ready to swallow her newborn baby the moment it arrives. This mirrors how Satan tried to kill Jesus right after his birth through wicked rulers like King Herod.

The woman gives birth to a son who is destined to rule all nations with an iron rod, meaning an unbreakable, shepherd-like rule. This child is Jesus Christ, who was snatched safely away from Satan's reach and taken up to God's heavenly throne. Because Jesus was rescued, the dragon's plot to destroy him completely failed.

After the child is taken up to heaven, the woman flees into a dry and lonely wilderness. God prepares a safe shelter for her and keeps her spiritually fed for 1,260 days. Even when the church seems hidden and oppressed in the world, God watches over her and preserves her life.

differ.view: The 1,260 days symbolize the whole present church age between Christ's first and second comings, during which God preserves his people.
John Wesley understood these prophetic days as 777 calendar years during which the true church found safe shelter in Europe, lasting from A.D. 847 until the Reformation in 1524.
This flight happens during a future seven-year period of trouble, when the Jewish remnant flees for safety to a desert place such as Petra for 1,260 literal days.

notes.meaning: A fierce battle breaks out in heaven between the archangel Michael and his holy angels against the dragon and his evil angels. The dragon fights back with all his might, but he is not strong enough to win. He loses the struggle, and no place is left for him or his demons in heaven.

The giant dragon is thrown out of heaven and cast down to the earth along with all his rebellious followers. John identifies him as the ancient serpent from the Garden of Eden, the devil, which means slanderer, and Satan, which means adversary. His main craft has been tricking the whole human race, but his power in heaven is broken.

A triumphant voice in heaven praises God because his salvation, strength, and Christ's kingdom have now arrived in full view. The devil has been hurled down, ending his hateful practice of accusing believers day and night before God. His slanders against God's people can no longer stand in God's presence.

differ.view: Satan was cast out and silenced through Christ's death and resurrection, meaning believers are already fully free from his accusations before God.
Satan still has access to accuse believers in heaven today, and this final expulsion will take place during a future time of tribulation.

notes.meaning: God's people gain the victory over Satan through the blood of Jesus, the Lamb who died in their place. They also overcome him by boldly telling the truth about what Jesus has done for them. They love Christ far more than their own comfort, willingly facing death rather than giving up their faith.

Heaven and everyone living in it are told to rejoice because the devil has been thrown out forever. Yet a terrible warning goes out to the earth and sea, because the devil has landed there in boiling anger. He rages fiercely because he knows his remaining time to tempt and harm people is very short.

Seeing that he has been cast down to the earth, the dragon vents his fury against the woman who bore the male child. Since he can no longer attack the ascended Savior in heaven, he attacks the church still living on earth. This hatred explains why believers have faced fierce persecution throughout world history.

God provides the woman with two wings like a great eagle so she can swiftly fly to her place of safety in the wilderness. This picture recalls how God carried ancient Israel out of Egypt and guarded them in the desert. In that hidden shelter, God sustains the church out of the serpent's reach for three and a half times, or years.

Unable to catch the woman, the serpent spits a river of water out of his mouth to sweep her away in a rushing flood. This flood pictures a wave of cruel attacks, invading enemies, or poisonous false teachings meant to wipe out the church. God steps in by causing the earth to open its mouth and swallow the river, showing that even natural events and worldly powers are guided by God to protect his people.

Furious that he cannot destroy the whole church, the dragon turns his anger against the rest of her children. These faithful individuals are defined as those who obey God's commands and stay true to the message of Jesus. Even though Satan cannot defeat God's kingdom, he continues to wage spiritual war against ordinary Christians everywhere.

differ.view: The rest of her offspring refers either to physical Jewish descendants who turn to God or to Gentiles who accept Christ during the coming Tribulation.
